chapter: New Orleans second line and Armstrong
title: Lawn parties and National Park in New Orleans
summary: He only peeped at Miss Cole's lawn parties as a child, and explains National Park was a baseball park used for dances.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I was going to ask you again to change the subject. We'll finish up in a few minutes now. About some of the New Orleans places like Miss Cole's Lawn Parties. Did you ever go there or were you just a kid?

I just peeped at them. They wouldn't allow me in there. They wouldn't allow me in there. I just peeped at them. But I did go to the National Park and dance by Joe's music before I was acquainted with Joe.
Was it the- Then we had that old second line too. You heard about the second line.
I want to ask about the phrase, let's talk a minute about the National Park. Was that for dances or did they play for ball?
Did they play for baseball games too? They put a platform down.
No they might advertise a baseball game. Very seldom there.
Would that be at night time or day time? The baseball game? No I mean when Joe would play there.
